summary: Christiane Antoine's unfinished chemistry note (draft, 19 Jun 2019) comparing three small-scale work-ups used on the coupling trials, with the assay stock and working concentrations, the solvent recovery question and open questions. Units are mixed in places, and a reviewer has marked up two sentences.

blocks.p: This note compares the small-scale work-ups we have used for the coupling trials over the spring. It is a working draft and several sections are incomplete.
The aim is to choose one work-up for the scale-up before the next analogue set is started. Nothing here is a final recommendation.

The quench and extraction steps differ between the three work-ups. Work-up A uses saturated sodium bicarbonate and ethyl acetate; work-up B uses water and dichloromethane; work-up C is a direct evaporation with a silica plug.

blocks.p: Work-up B gives the cleanest phase split. It also uses the most solvent, and the DCM goes to the halogenated waste stream unless it is recovered.

list.text: Work-up C not yet run at the larger scale

blocks.p: Stock solutions were made at 10 mM in DMSO. Working solutions for the assay were 50 µM in buffer, with a top concentration of 10 µM in the dose plate.
In the bench sheet the working solution is written as 50 nM in one place, while the protocol says 50 µM. Check the sheet before the next run.
Solubility of the crude products was checked at 5 mg/mL and 5 mg/ml in two different batches of DMSO and recorded without comparison.
Solvent recovery from the ethyl acetate washes is still undecided. The rotary evaporator in the back room is booked for the mixed-solvent fractions, so the washes may need to go to the waste stream.
Ask facilities whether the bump trap is fitted on the second unit. Until that is answered, do not plan recovery runs for the larger scale.
Which work-up goes forward for the scale-up? This is still open.
